To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal structure of an atypically folded α-phosphogucomutase from the HADSF has been determined and its mechanism of action has been elucidated.
the structure of the first α-phosphoglutamutase related to phosphomannomtases has been determined at 1,5 Å resolution.

the crystal structure of the atypical α-phosphate-glucomutase from L. lactis has been determined at high resolution and contains a glycerol and a sulfate bound at the enzyme catalytic site, which mimic the substrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, evolution and biotechnological applications of phosphomannomuteses and related enzymes.

the elucidation of the structure, the function and the catalytic mechanism of a bacterial α-D-phosphogluco-1-mutase, a member of the haloacid-dehalogenase super-family, which is the first member of this super-family that has an overall structure similar to that of eukaryotic D-phosphomannomutase.
a novel member of the α-phosphoglutomutase super-family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HADSF has evolved to catalyze a broad range of reactions and to use a broad range of substrates.
APGM is the first bacterial α-phosphohexose 1-mutase with a fold similar to that of eukaryotic α-phosphomannomutase.
APGM is a member of the HADSF, but that its active site is more related to the eukaryotic PMM2 than to other members of the HAD superfamily.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of APGM provides a basis for a detailed analysis of the molecular basis of substrate specificity within the HADSF.
APGM is the first structure of a HADSF enzyme with an α-D-phosphogluco configuration at the active site.
the structure of APGM, which is the first structure of an α-phosphoglcumutase related to the eukaryotic PMMs, is reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
APGM is the first bacterial α-phosphoglucumutase with an atypical overall fold and that its structure is similar to that of eukaryotic α-phosphomannomutase.

the structure of APGM is the first of a bacterial α-D-phosphogluco-mutase belonging to HADSF subclass IIb, and that it is the first structure of an α-phosphoglcumutase with an α/β fold similar to euryarchaeal and eukaryotic enzymes.

the APGM structure represents a novel type of α-phosphohexose mutase that is related to eukarylotic phosphomannose mutase and is the first structure of a member of the HADSF with an active site similar to that of the α-D-phosohexomutases.
